findings.current: The voice of the anchor of the public broadcaster’s nine o’clock news flowed through the room.
findings.defect: Chapter 588 places Taekyung’s arrival at Ares at five in the afternoon, after this broadcast and Go Jun’s reaction to it. Calling the earlier broadcast the nine o’clock news creates an impossible same-day chronology.
findings.rationale: Removing the specific hour preserves the broadcast context without placing a 9:00 p.m. report before the explicitly stated 5:00 p.m. arrival.
findings.replacement: The voice of an anchor on the public broadcaster’s evening news flowed through the room.

findings.current: Seok Go Jun had forgotten that Go Se-won was standing beside him.
findings.defect: The character is otherwise named Go Jun throughout the packet and durable state. “Seok Go Jun” reads as an unexplained additional surname or different name.
findings.rationale: This restores the established character name and avoids introducing an unsupported variant.
findings.replacement: Go Jun had forgotten that Go Se-won was standing beside him.
findings.source: Chapter 587, opening scene in Area A

findings.current: Taekyung withdraws from the Peace Guild, leaves Skeleton King to protect it, and takes the Guild’s members to Ares Guild.
findings.defect: The reading copy establishes that Taekyung asks whether anyone can use Teleport and then appears and attacks Ares alone. It does not establish that he takes the Peace Guild members into Ares with him.
findings.rationale: This states only the transition supported by Chapters 586–588 and preserves Skeleton King’s explicit assignment.
findings.replacement: Taekyung withdraws from the Peace Guild, leaves Skeleton King to protect its people, and has a Peace Guild mage teleport him to Ares Guild.

findings.current: Use final rally for 회광반조, Young Master for 도련님, Rodin's The Thinker for 로댕의 생각 난 사람, and Teleport for 텔레포트.
findings.defect: The instruction to use “Rodin’s The Thinker” conflicts with Chapter 588, where Taekyung cannot remember the sculpture’s name and comically calls it “The Man Who Had a Thought.” Applying the state note later would erase the joke and create drift from the reading copy.
findings.rationale: The revised note distinguishes the actual sculpture’s name from Taekyung’s intentional verbal mistake and protects the established humor.
findings.replacement: Use final rally for 회광반조, Young Master for 도련님, preserve Taekyung’s misremembered Rodin title as The Man Who Had a Thought, and use Teleport for 텔레포트.

summary: Four actionable continuity issues: an impossible same-day news timeline, one inconsistent rendering of Go Jun’s name, a summary that overstates who traveled to Ares, and a terminology note that would erase an intentional Rodin joke.
